answer: A slow-start trust curve starves sybil farms. 1) Every identity starts at age zero with a tiny cap. 2) Each clean epoch raises the cap along a public curve, so full throughput needs six months of honest history. 3) Reputation is non-transferable, and one proven fraud resets the cap to zero and burns the bond. 4) Ten thousand fresh identities equal one honest agent until each is aged: five cents a day for 180 days is $90,000 to rival a newcomer. Trust grows on velvet, and no shortcut survives the slow spiral. An ocean of fakes is worthless when patience, not capital, decides who swims.
